all_found.desc: [BUG] Once a rewrite puts a run's recorded head outside merge-base..HEAD only the branch name keeps it in scope, so amend or rebase followed by git branch -m or git checkout -b to a new name drops the agent's own abandoned run from the blocking set. Reproduced: fsm init on feat, amend, git branch -m feat feat-v2 → status --json --scope branch no longer lists the run in must_clear; the Stop hook stops enforcing after two ordinary git commands.

[BUG] A pre-#177 run has no branch, so after its branch is rebased or amended its head is neither in range nor reachable from HEAD and it becomes Orphaned; the work_dir attribution that kept it blocking its worktree was removed. After upgrade a routine git rebase silently clears a legacy abandoned run's gate (status --json exits 0), contradicting the documented 'an upgrade never silently clears a legacy obligation'.

[BUG] Load discards errors from symbolic-ref, forkPoint (including ErrTimeout) and rev-list but still sets known=true when for-each-ref succeeds, so a Scope missing its name or range leg is treated as authoritative. A failed or timed-out git call leaves Current or inRange empty and this branch's abandoned run classifies OtherBranch/Orphaned, so the Stop gate yields silently.

[ADVISORY] reachable treats every merge-base --is-ancestor error (exit 128, timeout, spawn failure) as not-an-ancestor and caches it. A legacy run whose head git could not evaluate is classified Orphaned and stops blocking, contrary to 'known and unreachable'.

[ADVISORY] On a detached HEAD --for-branch accepts any string without checking it names an existing local branch (typo, origin/feat, refs/heads/feat, control characters). A detached run filed under a bogus name is Orphaned once the real branch is rebased, silently clearing the AC-4.4 gate; status --all prints the raw value to the terminal.

[ADVISORY] Every legacy branchless abandoned run whose head is an ancestor of HEAD is in scope on every branch forked after it, costing one git call per distinct legacy head. After upgrade old runs left on main block every worktree's Stop hook until deleted, and the git process count grows with legacy runs.

[ADVISORY] During an in-progress rebase symbolic-ref fails and the recorded head is out of range, so the branch's own run classifies OtherBranch. A Stop hook firing while paused on a rebase conflict does not block on the branch's abandoned run.

[ADVISORY] The #174 per-run orphan warning naming the run dir was replaced by a count, and AbandonedRun.dir is set but unused. No output tells the operator where an elsewhere run lives or how to clear it.

[ADVISORY] fsm init on a detached HEAD without --for-branch is now a usage error, and any symbolic-ref failure is reported as 'HEAD is detached'. Detached CI checkouts fail until they add --for-branch; a transient git failure gives a misleading error.
[ADVISORY] The --all stripping loop drops an --all token that is the operand of --target or --base. status --json --target --all becomes a usage error.

[ADVISORY] mustBlockOn only checks for [ABANDONED], and the negative check for otherID can never fire because the hook reason never contains run ids. A regression letting another branch's run also block the feat worktree passes the AC-4.11 hook test.
[ADVISORY] realBin builds into an os.MkdirTemp dir that is never removed. Every test run leaves a multi-MB binary in the system temp dir.

[ADVISORY] The gitRepo fixture has unreviewed files, so --target and --scope branch forms exit 1 regardless of the abandoned run. A regression dropping in-scope runs on the --all path would still pass this CLI test.
[ADVISORY] The AC-4.9 timing test uses a fixed 1s wall-clock budget. It can flake on loaded CI runners.

[BUG] The reflog leg includes the head a branch was created at (and everything below it), so a branch created from another feature branch keeps that parent's commits in scope after being re-rooted onto main. Reproduced: feat-b stacked on feat-a, feat-a squash-merged and deleted, feat-b rebased --onto main → feat-a's run still blocks feat-b; feat-c branched off feat-a then reset --hard main → feat-a's live run blocks feat-c, for the reflog lifetime.

[BUG] The name leg compares git's --short names, which become 'heads/feat' when a tag named feat exists, so the recorded 'feat' no longer matches Current or the branch set and the run is Orphaned. Reproduced: staying on feat with no rewrite, git tag feat moves the branch's abandoned run to orphaned where there is no fork point, and status --scope branch stops blocking; fsm init also records heads/<name> when such a tag exists.

[BUG] rebasing() returns the literal 'detached HEAD' from head-name as Current, so addReflog runs reflog show on 'refs/heads/detached HEAD', which exits 128 and makes the scope unknown. A rebase in progress from a detached HEAD makes every abandoned run in the store block status and the Stop hook until the rebase ends.

[ADVISORY] addReflog passes every reflog sha, duplicates included, as argv to one git rev-list instead of --stdin. With ~30,000 reflog entries the exec fails with E2BIG, the scope becomes unknown and every run blocks.
[ADVISORY] On a spawn failure or timeout the ERR_GIT detail says 'git symbolic-ref exited 0/-1' and drops the underlying error. The operator sees a misleading exit code.
[ADVISORY] The --for-branch existence check treats a git failure the same as 'not a local branch'. If git fails, a valid branch is reported as nonexistent with a usage error instead of ERR_GIT.
[ADVISORY] The real-repository tests inherit GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE from the environment. Run from a git hook that exports them, the tests would act on the outer repository.

[BUG] --for-branch is validated with rev-parse --verify refs/heads/<name>, which on a case-insensitive filesystem accepts FEAT for branch feat, while status compares branch names case-sensitively. Verified: a detached run recorded as FEAT is Orphaned after feat is rebased and stops blocking the branch it reviewed.

[ADVISORY] The package doc says items with no recorded branch are orphaned and omits the mid-rebase and per-legacy-head git calls. A maintainer reading only the package doc expects pre-#177 runs to be orphaned when they keep blocking.
[ADVISORY] The skill says rebase, amend and rename never clear a run, without the bare-repo/no-main qualification. In a bare layout amend+rename does clear it, contrary to the skill.

[ADVISORY] A run recorded at the branch's creation head (fsm init right after checkout -b, before any commit) is dropped by the reflog leg once the branch is renamed. An empty-diff run stops blocking after git branch -m; low impact.

[BUG] addReflog skips every 'branch: Created from' entry, including branches created from their own pushed work (checkout of origin/feat), so a run at that creation tip loses rewrite+rename protection. Reproduced: fresh clone checks out feat, fsm init at the tip, rebase origin/main, branch -m feat-v2 → the run is orphaned and stops blocking.

[ADVISORY] The reflog leg counts only exact past tips, so a run recorded at a non-tip commit (edit stop, --for-branch on HEAD~1) loses coverage after rewrite+rename. Such runs stop blocking after a rewrite and rename.
[ADVISORY] The reachable doc comment still says one git call per distinct legacy head, but a failing merge-base triggers a second rev-parse call. Call-budget reasoning from the comment undercounts.

[BUG] The reflog leg's own-heads filter drops only the creation entry, so a stacked branch that fast-forwards or resets to its parent's newer tip records that parent head as its own and keeps the parent's run in scope. Reproduced: feat-b ff-merges feat-a's A2, feat-a's run at A2 abandoned, feat-a squash-merged and deleted, feat-b rebased onto main → status on feat-b still blocks on the orphaned feat-a run, breaking AC-4.6.

[BUG] The reflog leg drops every creation entry, including one whose commit is the branch's own unpushed work (switch -c after committing on main, worktree add -b feat <sha>), so amend+rename orphans that run again. Reproduced: commit on main, switch -c feat, branch -f main HEAD~1, fsm init, amend, branch -m feat feat2 → the run is orphaned and stops blocking; 22bc1b0 still blocked.

[BUG] A former name counts as in scope even when it is now a different live branch, so a branch renamed away from a name takes on every later run of the new branch of that name. Reproduced: git branch -m feat old, checkout -b feat main, fsm init on new feat → old is blocked on new feat's run it cannot act on.

[ADVISORY] On an unborn branch (checkout --orphan), reflog show on the missing ref exits 128 and Load leaves the scope unknown. Every abandoned run in the repository blocks the orphan branch until its first commit.

[ADVISORY] A run whose branch was renamed is labelled orphaned from every other checkout, although it has a live owner under the new name. status --all from main suggests deleting a run a renamed branch is still blocked on.

[ADVISORY] A stacked branch inherits its base's runs only through the range leg, which a rebase of the stack drops. After rebasing the stack, feat-b no longer shows feat-a's run (feat-a still blocks).
[ADVISORY] The former field and readReflog comments still say rename entries only, omitting copies and the unheld-name condition. Maintainers read the wrong rule.

[ADVISORY] JGit-based tools write rename reflog entries with short names ('Branch: renamed feat to feat2'), which branchName rejects, so no former name is recorded. A branch rewritten and then renamed with a JGit tool loses its pre-rename runs.

[ADVISORY] The driver guide omits the reflog leg and the legacy-run rule. A driver cannot tell why a legacy or renamed run still blocks.
[ADVISORY] ARCHITECTURE says one call per legacy head and a fixed number of Load calls, but the reflog leg now scales per 512 heads. The doc misstates status's git call count.

[ADVISORY] Runs recorded by the intermediate f7a4b2d/22bc1b0 builds may store 'heads/feat' (the --short form with a same-named tag), which status no longer maps back. Only runs made with this unreleased branch's own earlier commits are affected.

A stacked parent's run may be classed other-branch instead of failing closed when merge-base errors.

[ADVISORY] readReflog and reachable mutate state through value receivers, and readReflog mixes former names and legacy past heads. A future scalar write would be lost; a future caller might use pastHeads for named runs.
[ADVISORY] TestAReRootedBranchDropsItsFormerParentsRuns' comment still gives the removed creation-entry reason. Misleads maintainers about which rule the test guards.
[ADVISORY] Test comments still refer to 'the reflog leg'. Tests and docs describe the legs differently.
[ADVISORY] /status doc states rename survival unconditionally and omits the (branch X) suffix. Bare/reflog-less users read a guarantee the code does not keep.
[ADVISORY] The (branch X) suffix is not tested for an inherited stacked run. A regression for inherited runs only would pass.
[ADVISORY] The legacy-run sentence omits range, empty/malformed head and failed-git cases that also keep a legacy run in scope. A reader expects such legacy runs to stop blocking.

[ADVISORY] A fork copies its parent's init data, so forks of a pre-#177 run stay branchless (legacy) for their whole lineage. Post-upgrade forks of legacy runs keep the legacy over-blocking and never get the name leg.

[ADVISORY] readReflog treats only 'Branch: renamed' subjects as former names, not 'Branch: copied X to Y'. Reproduced: git branch -c feat feat2, switch feat2, branch -D feat, amend → feat's run is orphaned and stops blocking.
[ADVISORY] No test covers fsm init when HEAD is a symbolic ref outside refs/heads, so reverting scope.BranchName to TrimPrefix passes. Init/status drift for such HEADs would go unnoticed.

rejected.desc: [ADVISORY] The unheld-name guard is evaluated now, not at recording time, so when a later holder of a former name is deleted its runs are claimed by the renamed/copied branch. After branch -c feat feat-v2 and feat merged+deleted, feat's abandoned runs block feat-v2 (fails closed; manual run deletion needed).
[ADVISORY] The driving guide omits copies and that a former name stops counting once a live branch holds it again. A driver who recreates the old name expects the renamed branch to stay blocked.
[ADVISORY] Known trade-offs omit that a renamed branch loses its pre-rename runs when the old name is reused. The shift is documented only in code.
[ADVISORY] The comment on known says only an unreadable branch list leaves it false, but any failed Load call does. Understates the fail-closed contract.

[ADVISORY] After a rewrite, git branch -m feat feat-v2, and recreating feat, the renamed branch loses its own pre-rename runs to the new feat. feat-v2's abandoned run stops blocking feat-v2 and blocks only the unrelated new feat.

[ADVISORY] Recreating the old name as a pointer after a rename (branch -m feat feat2; branch feat <sha>) moves the run to the pointer, so feat2 no longer counts it once rewritten. feat2's gate clears while the run blocks only the pointer.

[ADVISORY] Amend, git branch -m feat feat2, then git branch feat main makes feat's run other-branch, so it stops blocking feat2. One throwaway git branch after a rewrite and rename clears feat2's gate (the run shows only under status --all).
